content.text: dois estudantes, Kate e Ben, e a tutora, Dr. Hughes, discutem um projeto sobre desperdício de comida no campus.
What do Kate and Ben disagree about at first?
A) the topic B) the method C) the deadline
Why does Ben prefer to observe the cafeteria?
A) It's cheaper. B) People don't always tell the truth in surveys. C) The tutor told him to.
What does Dr. Hughes say about their sample?
A) It's too small. B) It's too large. C) It's fine.
What do they finally decide to do?
A) observation only B) survey only C) both
A) contact the cafeteria manager B) write the questionnaire C) read previous studies
So, for our project on food waste, I think a survey of students is the obvious choice.
I'm not so sure. People say they don't waste food, but then they throw half their lunch away. I'd rather observe what actually happens in the cafeteria.
I see what you mean, but observation takes so much time.
Both methods have value. But you mentioned surveying thirty students — that won't tell you much about a campus of eight thousand.
We could aim for two hundred online.
Much better. And Ben's point about honesty is important.
What if we do both? A survey to see what people think, and two days of observation to compare.
OK, I'm convinced. It'll make the results more interesting.
Good. Remember you'll need permission to observe in the cafeteria.
Right, I'll email the manager today, before we do anything else. Ben, could you start on the questions?
